requirements.text: Planning gate pass requires every approved decision row, requirement id, and downstream planning question to map to executable work, sprint scope, accepted deferral, no-work rationale, or implementation evidence.
Planning must reconcile existing roadmap tasks/sprints against newly accepted decisions before creating new work or passing planning gate.
Accepted target state with no implementation evidence, owner work, or deferral produces planning-gate remediation and remains in planning until superseding planning accounts for it.
Trace/planning evidence must carry decision coverage and roadmap reconciliation links from decision rows to planning, roadmap, implementation, and gate verdicts.
Accepted loop-first/source restructure must be replanned into active atomic tasks/sprint scope or explicit accepted deferrals; roadmap open=0 is not sufficient.

summary: Accepted decision-to-planning gate hardening: planning gates must enforce complete decision coverage, existing-roadmap reconciliation, trace-linked requirement/work mapping, and immediate replanning of accepted source restructure deltas.

decision_table.title: Accepted decision-to-planning gate hardening: planning gates must enforce complete decision coverage, existing-roadmap reconciliation, trace-linked requirement/work mapping, and immediate replanning of accepted source restructure deltas.

rows.question: DTP-001

state_delta.current: Planning can pass while accepted decision rows are only partially mapped to executable work or deferrals; later roadmap can show open=0 even when target system state remains unimplemented.
state_delta.desired: Every approved decision row and downstream planning question must be planned into executable work, sprint scope, accepted deferral with owner/trigger, or explicit no-work rationale before planning gate pass. If coverage is incomplete, the planning gate returns findings/remediation and the planning loop continues with a superseding planning output.

rows.proposed_change: Every approved decision row/question needs planning coverage; incomplete coverage yields planning-gate remediation and a superseding planning output.
rows.rationale: This is the direct failure mode that hid the loop-first/source restructure gap.

risk.notes: medium: stricter planning gates may return more remediation findings.

rows.expected_outcome: Planning gate pass means all decision rows/questions are accounted for; fail/block means continue planning with exact remediation, not stop or lose the decision.

rows.question: DTP-002

state_delta.current: Planning primarily creates or updates tasks for the new decision; it does not reliably re-evaluate existing roadmap tasks/sprints against the newly accepted desired state.
state_delta.desired: Planning must consider replanning the existing roadmap whenever a decision creates or changes work: refine existing tasks, reopen/cancel superseded work, update sprint scope/order, or create new tasks only when boundaries are atomic and not duplicates.

rows.proposed_change: Planning must reconcile existing roadmap before creating or passing new planning outputs.
rows.rationale: New decisions can invalidate current roadmap shape.

risk.notes: medium: replanning can alter task lifecycle and needs trace evidence.

rows.expected_outcome: Existing roadmap work is refined, split, reopened, cancelled, superseded, reordered, or rescoped when accepted decisions change target state.

rows.question: DTP-003

state_delta.current: Planning/closure evidence can treat warning coverage, cancelled aggregate tasks, or residual deferrals as enough even when accepted target architecture still lacks active owner tasks.
state_delta.desired: Planning gate must return a fail/block finding with remediation when accepted target state has no current implementation evidence and no active/closed owner work or approved deferral with owner/trigger. The planning loop then continues until a superseding planning output accounts for the target state; open=0 cannot mean done when accepted target structure remains unmatched.

rows.proposed_change: Accepted target states without owner coverage produce planning-gate remediation and remain in planning until planned, deferred, or proven implemented.
rows.rationale: Prevents accepted restructure from disappearing after cleanup tasks close, while preserving gate finding as loop-continuation feedback.

risk.notes: medium-high: better matching may surface historical gaps.

rows.expected_outcome: Accepted target states do not become silent open=0 residuals.

rows.question: DTP-004

state_delta.current: Trace-primary docs exist, but decision rows, planning work units, roadmap tasks, implementation evidence, and gate verdicts are not yet enforced as one traceability chain.
state_delta.desired: Planning builds/traces must assign requirement ids from decision rows to work units/tasks/sprints, and planning gate must verify trace links from decision -> planning -> roadmap coverage. Traceability matrix/graph should expose unmapped, deferred, superseded, and implemented states.

rows.proposed_change: Trace/planning evidence must carry decision coverage and roadmap reconciliation links.
rows.rationale: Trace is the accountability mechanism to prevent decisions being lost or overmerged.

risk.notes: medium: schema/source changes and legacy compatibility needed.

rows.expected_outcome: Traceability matrix/graph exposes unmapped, deferred, superseded, implemented, and replanned states.

rows.question: DTP-005

state_delta.current: Accepted loop-first/source restructure remains represented in KB target structure, but no active roadmap owner exists after cleanup tasks closed.
state_delta.desired: After this decision passes, planning must reconcile accepted restructure targets into an active sprint/task plan or explicit accepted deferrals. Remaining source-root migrations must not be left as open=0 residual state.

rows.proposed_change: Immediate accepted source restructure gap must be replanned into atomic tasks/sprint scope or explicit deferrals.
rows.rationale: Addresses the immediate instance while systemic gate behavior is fixed.

risk.notes: medium-high: broad restructure must be split into atomic tasks with compatibility gates.

rows.expected_outcome: Remaining source-root migrations have active owner tasks/sprint scope, implementation evidence, or accepted deferrals.
